name: Justice Defenders
mission: JUSTICE DEFENDERS PROVIDES LEGAL EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND PRACTICE WITHIN DEFENSELESS COMMUNITIES. FOUNDED IN 2007, JUSTICE DEFENDERS WORK ACROSS 35+ PRISONS IN AFRICA WHERE INCARCERATED PEOPLE AND OFFICERS TRAIN AND PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES FOR THEMSELVES AND OTHERS.
theoryOfChange: Justice Defenders has a published theory of change as part of their 'The Justice Defenders Way' document on their official website. This document outlines their 2025-2027 strategy, which includes expanding their work to '10 new prisons. Including planting a prison community in the United States.' The document explicitly states 'OUR THEORY OF CHANGE' under 'Our founding documents'. The 'The Justice Defenders Way' page describes their approach to bringing justice to those in need through legal education, training, and practice within prison communities, aiming to transform prisons into places of learning and service.

In 2024 alone, their legal support contributed to <cite id="4">15,338 prisoner releases ordered by courts</cite> and <cite id="4">2,032 releases via alternative dispute resolution</cite>. rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2007, Justice Defenders provides legal education, paralegal training, and legal representation to incarcerated individuals and prison staff in East Africa <cite id="3">to ensure fair access to justice</cite>. The organization operates primarily in Kenya and Uganda, equipping prisoners to advocate for themselves and others within the legal system. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="2">Total Revenue of $1,331,729</cite>, representing a decline from $1,868,837 in FY2023. The organization maintains an <cite id="1">overall Charity Navigator score of 82.0/100</cite>. While Justice Defenders demonstrates significant program outcomes—such as over <cite id="4">15,000 prisoners released by the courts</cite> reported in 2024—it faces financial operational headwinds. Specifically, its <cite id="1">Program Expense Ratio was 58.5% in FY2024</cite>, which sits below the 75% standard benchmark, and officer compensation represents a noticeable share of total revenue. Overall, the charity presents a unique model of paralegal training within prisons alongside notable administrative and spending tradeoffs.
